title: One-step addition
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a program, $m$ a memory, and $i,j,k,a,b$ integers. If the program beginning at position $pos$ starts with the instruction that adds the contents of addresses $j$ and $k$ into address $i$, and the words at $j$ and $k$ represent $a$ and $b$, respectively, then one step from $(pos,m)$ reaches program counter $pos+1$ and memory equal to $m$ updated at address $i$ with the word representing $a+b$.
hypotheses_covered: The program at pos begins with add i j k
m(j) is the W-bit representation of a
m(k) is the W-bit representation of b
